hypothesis: If the Glacial period was long-lasting and at least in part simultaneous worldwide, a globally mixed marine proxy (benthic d18O) must show prolonged cold/ice-rich intervals lasting well over 10 kyr, with a high-d18O state at the last glacial maximum.
pass_criterion: In the LR04 stack (age in ka, benthic d18O in per mil), all three hold: (1) d18O >= 4.0 per mil during at least 20% of 0-2600 ka (linear-interpolated time); (2) at least 5 separate contiguous intervals >= 4.0 per mil each lasting >= 10 kyr; (3) mean d18O over 18-26 ka >= 4.5 per mil.
fail_criterion: Any one of these: d18O >= 4.0 per mil covers less than 10% of 0-2600 ka; fewer than 2 contiguous intervals >= 4.0 per mil last >= 10 kyr; or the 18-26 ka mean d18O is below 4.2 per mil. Results between the pass and fail thresholds are reported as inconclusive.
interpretation: Darwin's Glacial period is mapped to Pleistocene glacial stages. Simultaneous worldwide cooling is mapped to the benthic d18O signal (ice volume plus deep-water temperature), which is globally mixed and recorded in 57 cores on one common age model. This is a modern reinterpretation and a weaker proxy for the simultaneity part of the claim. A global stack shows that a global cold state occurred for long durations, but it cannot resolve regional phase lags or the longitudinal-belt version. Darwin implied one long glacial episode, whereas the data show many cycles. The test therefore asks only whether long globally cold intervals recur. Thresholds of 4.0 and 4.5 per mil are set from the approximate glacial/interglacial range of the stack and are fixed before analysis.

dataset.name: Pliocene-Pleistocene stack of globally distributed benthic stable oxygen isotope records
dataset.why_it_fits: The LR04 stack averages benthic d18O from 57 globally distributed deep-sea cores on a common age scale. The age (ka) and benthic d18O columns give the duration and recurrence of the global cold state, and the error column supports sensitivity checks.
